On Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 9:12 AM Kevin Adams <kevin.adams@novahealth.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a major spike in 5xx and 429s across our traffic to Redwood starting ~08:45 PT...

Triage summary:
- Root cause (initial): sudden client-side retry amplification from NovaHealth after a transient slowdown in their network. Their client retries were very aggressive (no jitter, short backoff) which pushed sustained concurrency above our tenant soft-limits, causing head-of-line queuing and model-worker saturation.
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx (~4%) and 429s; RPC timeouts; increased tail latency for affected model variants.
- Evidence: tenant throughput and queue depth graphs (uploaded to drive), PD incident PD-9221, and traces show repeated identical requests from a small set of NovaHealth IPs.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:24–09:30 PT):
1) Applied temporary per-tenant ingress throttle for NovaHealth to 60% of their baseline traffic (reduces queue pressure).
2) Disabled the heavy-ensemble model variant for their tenant and routed to a lower-cost variant with similar quality to keep latency down.
3) Manually increased serving pool by spinning an additional dedicated worker ring for 30m to drain queues.

Status: Error rates dropping but still above SLO; continuing to monitor. Created Jira CRQ-1298 to track mitigation and permanent fixes (adaptive tenant backpressure, improved client guidance on retry backoff).

Next steps:
- Laura to run correlation on other customers to ensure this was limited to NovaHealth.
- Markus to propose SLO tuning and per-tenant throttling policy changes by EOD.

I'll keep updating — Dev

Team — quick exec update for context.

Customer impact: NovaHealth reported failures in production (ingestion and batch jobs). We observed tenant-specific queueing due to retry amplification that escalated to a platform SLO breach. Our mitigations have reduced load and errors are trending downward; final stabilty expected within 2–3 hours.

Customer request: NovaHealth asked for an estimated time-to-stable and asked to escalate to an exec contact for SLA credit discussion.

Proposed immediate customer-facing commitments:
- Confirm stabilization and send a timeline and short RCA within 48 hours.
- Offer a discretionary credit (one month pro-rata) contingent on RCA and remediation plan sign-off.

Ask to leadership: please confirm approval to offer the above credit if the RCA supports our mitigation was necessary. Also signoff to open a postmortem and schedule a 1:1 with NovaHealth engineering leadership tomorrow.

I'll draft the customer update once we have stabilization confirmation.

— Hannah

Subject: Postmortem draft & action tracker — NovaHealth 2027-04-21 flare

Attached is the postmortem draft (novahealth_postmortem.pdf) and the proposed mitigation RFC (rfc_retry_mitigation.md). Summary highlights and action items below:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2027-04-21 08:45–11:12 PT (majority of errors resolved by 10:40 PT after mitigations).
- Cause: client-driven retry amplification combined with insufficient per-tenant soft-limits and model-variant resource contention.
- What worked: quick application of tenant throttle and model-variant fallback; runbook execution to spin additional capacity.
- Gaps identified: missing alert for per-tenant queue depth (>90th percentile), runbook lacked clear instruction for tenant throttle thresholds, SLO per-tenant bucketing not granular enough.

Action items (owner — due):
1) Per-tenant queue-depth alert + dashboard (Markus Klein — 2027-05-05)
2) Update incident runbook with explicit throttle steps & thresholds (Laura Bennett — 2027-04-28)
3) Implement adaptive backpressure (CRQ-1298) and client guidance doc for exponential backoff (Dev Patel — 2027-05-12)
4) SLO tuning: evaluate per-tenant SLO bucketing and adjust soft-limits for large customers (Markus Klein — 2027-05-15)
5) Customer comms: finalize and send RCA + credit approval (Hannah Schmitt — 2027-04-23)
6) Capacity planning: evaluate long-tail peak needs and propose reserved burst pool (Stepha nie Nguyen — 2027-05-01)

Please review the attachments and flag any missing items. I'll push the final PDF to the Drive link and update CRQ-1298 with tasks.

Laura Bennett
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
